comment: Example client configs for laptops on the same LAN. Replace 'your-mac.local' with your host's mDNS name or LAN IP. The host serves FOUR lanes from one endpoint: 'orch' + 'flash' (cloud) and 'local-orch' + 'local-sub' (host GPU). A lane name is the stable contract - the host can swap the model behind it without any client edit. Point the main model at a driving lane ('orch' or 'local-orch') and the worker/subagent model at its cheap partner ('flash' or 'local-sub'). Client bootstrap also installs `opencode-cloud` (the cloud pair) and `opencode-local` (the GPU pair). Easiest of all: just run `ferry opencode` on the client to write the opencode block below automatically (it detects whatever the host is serving).

opencode._tip: Or just run `ferry opencode` on the client to write this automatically.

generic_openai_sdk_python.code:
from openai import OpenAI

client = OpenAI(
    base_url='http://your-mac.local:8090/v1',
    api_key='local'
)

response = client.chat.completions.create(
    model='orch',
    messages=[{'role': 'user', 'content': 'Tell me a joke.'}]
)
print(response.choices[0].message.content)
